# APIs and services

## Scope

Applies when the change touches HTTP, gRPC, events, webhooks. Not when the interface stays inside one process, such as an internal function signature. Neighbours: `aidd-team:api-design`, `aidd-team:product-defaults`, `aidd-team:performance`.

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A changed request, response, status code, event, GraphQL type, or Protobuf message is a contract change: never minor. | S1, S5 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Product defaults (`api_conventions`, `data_conventions`, `operability`): build each one `project.defaults.disabled` does not name, as `aidd-team:product-defaults` says. | — |
| Specify | The OpenAPI or AsyncAPI change, the GraphQL schema, or the `.proto` file is written before Spec approval and listed in `design.files`, so Spec approval freezes it. The Acceptance references its operations and schemas. | S1, S5 |
| Specify | Errors, idempotency, and versioning follow `aidd-team:api-design`. Rate limits, quotas, and spending limits on paid providers are stated (OWASP API4). | S2, S3 |
| Implement | Validate input against the contract at the boundary. Authorize per object and per property (OWASP API1, API3). Paginate every list. A GraphQL server caps depth and cost and takes only persisted operations from first-party clients. | S2, S5 |
| Implement | Webhooks are signed and carry an id and a timestamp; a receiver verifies them and drops a replay (Standard Webhooks). A sender resolves each target URL and refuses private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses, after each redirect too (OWASP API7). | S6, S2 |
| Implement | Real time: server-sent events for server-to-client updates, WebSocket only for two-way traffic. Each connection authenticates when it opens, sends heartbeats, bounds its send buffer, and resumes after a drop (SSE's `Last-Event-ID`, or a sequence number); fan-out across instances goes through a pub/sub channel. | S7, S8 |
| Implement | Tokens follow RFC 9700: no implicit or password grant, PKCE, exact redirect URIs, and short-lived or sender-constrained tokens. API keys are stored hashed, shown once, scoped, expiring, and prefixed so a secret scanner finds a leak. | S9 |
| Review | Only additive changes without a version bump. A removal follows `aidd-team:api-design`'s expand and contract and is recorded in the Spec's `deprecations`, so a passed sunset warns. | S4 |
| Roll out | Consumer contract tests pass for every known consumer before rollout. 4xx and 5xx rates and p95 latency are the observe signals; calls to deprecated operations are counted per consumer. | S1 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spectral | the OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document lints clean | `npx @stoplight/spectral-cli@6.17.0 lint openapi.yaml` in the test commands, with a `.spectral.yaml` of `extends: ["spectral:oas", "@stoplight/spectral-owasp-ruleset"]` (ruleset 2.0.1) unless an org preset names a shared one | S1 |
| Contract tests | every known consumer still passes against the head | consumer-driven, with Pact: each consumer's tests write its pact, and the provider verifies every consumer's pact against the head. The verification runs as a `tests.commands` entry (such as `npm run test:pact:verify`, or the stack's Pact verifier) with `when_changed` on the API code and its contract. At release: `pact-broker can-i-deploy --pacticipant <provider> --version <sha> --to-environment production` (pact_broker-client v1.78.0) | S1 |
| Schema conformance | the running API matches its contract | `uvx schemathesis==4.28.0 run <openapi-url>` against the running service | S1 |
| Breaking-change diff | no breaking API or event-schema change without a major version | `oasdiff breaking --fail-on ERR base.yaml openapi.yaml` (oasdiff v1.32.1), and for events `npx @asyncapi/cli@6.2.1 diff base.yaml asyncapi.yaml -t breaking`, where a small script writes `base.yaml` from the base commit (`git show <base>:<file>`) first, as a `tests.commands` entry with `when_changed` on the contract; a breaking change passes only with a major version, and a schema registry checks each new event schema against every earlier version (backward transitive) | S4 |
| GraphQL schema diff | no breaking GraphQL change without a major version, and every dangerous one named | `npx -p @graphql-inspector/cli@7.0.0 graphql-inspector diff base.graphql schema.graphql`, with `base.graphql` written from the base commit, as a `tests.commands` entry with `when_changed` on the schema | S5, S4 |
| Protobuf lint and breaking check | the `.proto` files lint clean and break no wire or JSON compatibility | `buf lint` and `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=<base>'` (buf v1.73.0), with `when_changed` on the `.proto` files | S4 |
| OWASP ZAP API scan | no high finding on the changed operations | `zap-api-scan.py` from the ZAP 2.17.0 image against a test deployment | S2 |
| Load test | the SLO holds under expected load | the load-test runner's `tests` entry, such as `k6 run`, with the SLO as thresholds that fail the run | — |

- From `aidd-team:product-defaults`: API conventions, Operability smoke.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
